newsitem.title: UK: Amoco starts new No. Sea natgas plant on Teesside.
newsitem.headline: Amoco starts new No. Sea natgas plant on Teesside.

text.p: Amoco (UK) Exploration Company on Wednesday announced the start up of a new multi-million pound gas processing plant on Teesside in northeast England, linking oil and gas fields in the central North Sea directly to national gas markets and providing feedstocks to local chemical industries.

The plant at Seal Sands in Billingham allows the Central Area Transmission System (CATS), the newest North Sea gas transport system, to add additional capacity to process and deliver gas into the National Transmission System operated by Transco, a division of BG plc.

It has been completed four months ahead of schedule, under budget and without a Lost Time Accident, and Amoco said in a statement that it makes Teesside a major hub for North Sea gas and the only area in the UK to receive associated gas liquids directly by pipeline. The first gas flowed through the system on May 6.

The CATS system, operational since 1993, has a capacity of more than 1.6 billion cubic feet a day of gas, meeting the requirements of over eight million typical British households. It consists of an offshore platform located in the Everest field, a 255 mile long, 36 inch diameter pipeline, and now an onshore reception and processing plant.
A second processing plant is under construction and will bring the processing capacity at the CATS terminal to 1.2 billion cubic feet a day on completion in mid-1998.

The new plant will process wet gas from the Everest and Lomond fields, and will provide both natural gas liquids (NGLs) and dry gas of the quality required for the National Transmission System. By October, volumes entering the plant are expected to reach 600 million cubic feet a day of gas and 1000 tonnes a day of NGLs when BG's Armada field and Texaco's Erskine field come onstream through CATS.

Throughput through CATS will increase again in 1998 to 1200 million cubic feet a day of gas and 2000 tonnes of NGLs when the BP-operated Eastern Trough Area Project (ETAP) complex is due to start production.
Gas flowing through CATS now comes from the Everest, Lomond and Andrew fields, with 300 million cubic feet a day of gas from Everest and Lomond fuelling a gas-fired power station on Teesside.
